answer.evidence: The chair is drawn in side profile facing east, with a tall backrest on the left (rows 1-13, exempt as seat_back) and a seat from row 9 to row 13 that is 11 px wide. Row 9 is the dark outline. The lighter band at rows 10-11 (L=157 at x=6, only row 10 at x=8) is 1-2 rows and has no front-edge line or eave shadow. It does not widen and narrow like an ellipse. Below it the seat shows a vertical face of mid and dark browns (rows 11-13, L 124 to 70), then legs at rows 14-15. The seat surface is therefore a thin strip of at most 2 rows, which is a rim and not a top surface, so the chair reads as front_elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate chair is a tiny, narrow sprite with only 7 distinct colours in total, against 14 for the bench and 38-40 for the stall and well. Its shading is shallow, about 3 steps of wood (a light edge, a mid tone and a dark outline), where the bench reference reads as 5 steps with slat highlights and grain. The dark edge pixels are 57% near-neutral, a mix of neutral and tinted. That leans toward the sticker look more than the bench (44%) and is far from the tinted outlines of the hedge and stall. The chair is smaller than one tile, so the per-tile facts are 0 and I judged by eye. It has no visible grain, knots or highlight variation on the seat or back, so it looks thinner and flatter than the bench next to it. A careful artist would not accept it beside the references without adding more shading and texture.
